articles.title: 'We Can't Afford Kathryn Hahn': VisionQuest Creator Explains Why Agatha Harkness Didn't Appear
articles.summary: VisionQuest creator Terry Matalas has explained why Agatha Harkness failed to appear on screen during the series — despite her presence being felt. Before its launch, VisionQuest was described as the concluding chapter of the WandaVision trilogy (which began with WandaVision, and continued with…
body: The finale of VisionQuest sees the return of Joe Locke's Billy Maximoff from Agatha All Along, as he reunites with Tommy Maximoff and his synthezoid sort-of father Vision. This picks up directly from WandaVision's final scene, where Billy sets off to go find his brother aided by a ghostly Harkness, who has now left her physical body behind.

While Agatha does not appear on screen in VisionQuest, Billy still talks briefly with her. Tommy even realizes that Billy is doing so, and makes a comment about his brother having an invisible friend — as Harkness does not appear to him (or the audience).

While it would have been great to see her physically (or spectrally) again, the dialogue is still a neat way of acknowledging her presence and confirming she's still helping Billy. But why not have Kathryn Hahn back for a cameo?

"We can't afford Kathryn Hahn!" Matalas told ScreenRant, acknowledging Hahn's absence. "First of all, the second you bring Kathryn Hahn into a scene, it's a Kathryn Hahn scene. It's really about Agatha, and in that moment of the reunion, it needed to be about Billy. [It] needed to be about Tommy.
points: VisionQuest creator Terry Matalas has explained why Agatha Harkness failed to appear on screen during the series — despite her presence being felt.

articles.title: AI Chat App Character.ai is Attempting to Stave Off Bankruptcy, And Has a $20 Million Offer From Disney
articles.summary: Character.ai went live in 2022, alongside many other AI apps like ChatGPT, forever changing the online landscape (for the worse, many would argue). While it never became a household name, like ChatGPT, Grok, or Gemini, Character.ai found its place in online fandom spaces.
body: It is no surprise, then, that the service ran into many legal and ethical issues. Some copyright holders would do what they could to have their characters removed from the service, and moderators would struggle to remove bots based on real people. More seriously, questions were raised about the safety measures in place to protect users, as at least two minors were found to have used Character.ai extensively before they died by suicide. This resulted in two lawsuits, one of which has since been settled.

Throughout all of this, Character.ai has been struggling to turn its sizeable user base into profit. Despite several attempts to turn this around — rolling out new features, ads, and testing out subscription fees — Character.ai has been unsuccessful and has now filed for bankruptcy.

In October, Disney came to the company's aid, paying $60 million to grab 66 of Character.ai's employees (as per Business Insider ). It has further proposed paying $20 million to acquire some of Character.ai's tech, leading to speculation that Disney is looking to enter the AI chatbot space, perhaps with its own copyrighted characters.

articles.title: Xbox Project Helix Is A Console That Plays PC Games, Not The Other Way Around
articles.summary: Xbox has revealed more details about its next-gen device, Project Helix, describing it as a "console capable of playing games from your PC." Prominently featured in the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine, VP of next-gen Jason Ronald said the Xbox Series X|S successor is designed to build on the…
body: Project Helix will also let "hardcore" gamers customize their gaming experience, but how much will all of this cost? Xbox isn't revealing a ballpark figure for Project Helix yet, but Ronald did mention the company is aiming to balance state-of-the-art gaming with an "affordable" price tag. Game preservation will also play a key role, letting users bring their Xbox library with them, and Ronald teased Project Helix as a brand that spans multiple facets of gaming, from living room experiences to handheld sessions and cloud streaming. As a sign of things to come, the Xbox mode on the recently released ROG Xbox Ally was mentioned as the direction the gaming division is headed.

The news on Project Helix comes at a time when Xbox has had several highs and lows throughout 2026. This year saw several first-party games release and earn plenty of acclaim, while the anniversary celebrations included a special-edition Xbox Series X that few people could get their hands on — for retail price, that is. At the same time, the rise of Asha Sharma as Xbox CEO has seen scores of jobs and studios slashed from the Xbox family as the company undergoes a "reset" aimed at making it more profitable.

articles.title: The next Xbox, Project Helix, is a console and "not a PC" says Microsoft, as it clarifies that computational power isn't sole focus this time
articles.summary: Microsoft has stressed that its next-generation Xbox console, Project Helix, "is not a PC that can also play console games", but rather "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC".
body: The details come from a Microsoft-produced Xbox magazine made available digitally yesterday, and a Helix-related feature speaking to Xbox vice president of next generation, Jason Ronald. "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine," Ronald said, "one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games.

Notably, Ronald seemed to suggest that Helix - the console, not the handheld; "Helix" refers to a couple of machines - isn't solely focused on computational grunt. Indeed, he said the next generation wasn't about hitting 8K resolutions and 240 hertz frame-rates, but instead leaning on technologies like "neural rendering" - i.e. generative-AI - and encouraging innovation.
points: Microsoft has stressed that its next-generation Xbox console, Project Helix, "is not a PC that can also play console games", but rather "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC".

Cyberagent boasted an 88 percent "hit" rate for its mobile releases so far, with seven of its eight releases having a development budget of around a billion yen, and reaching a point where it makes that figure back every month from its playerbases. articles.summary: Escape From Tarkov promo codes are used in the classic extraction shooter for all sorts of rewards. From in-game gear and weapons to currency, cosmetics, and more, redeeming as many of these Tarkov codes as you can will set you up for your next raid.
body: Here are all the currently active Escape From Tarkov promo codes, the rewards they grant, and how to redeem them in-game.

There are two ways to redeem promo codes in Escape From Tarkov. The first is to boot up the game launcher, then click on the drop-down arrow beneath your username in the top right-hand corner. Then select activate code and type in any of the codes listed above. If successful, you'll see green text telling you the reward has been claimed.

Alternatively, you can visit the official Escape From Tarkov promo code page on the website and type in the code there. Make sure you're signed in when you do so, and if you play Tarkov through Steam, ensure your account is linked.

articles.title: EA hires another former Call of Duty boss to take the lead on all Battlefield Studios' projects
articles.summary: EA has made some notable leadership changes within its studios group, and in who oversees the Battlefield franchise. Byron Beede, previously Battlefield's general manager, has been promoted to group general manager.
body: Beede announced the change on LinkedIn, saying that he now oversees EA's shooter and action-RPG portfolio, seemingly occupying the role of the late Vince Zampella.

In this stead, EA appointed Sam Cooper as Battlefield's new boss. Cooper, who also revealed his new job title on LinkedIn, previously had a stint at EA Sports, but he's mostly known for his work at Activision, where he spent the last five-ish years as Call of Duty's global product management and head of live service.

While this might seem like fairly unremarkable corporate news - executives move between rival companies all the time, after all - it reinforces a narrative that EA continues to keenly replicate Activision's Call of Duty model.

That particular push is years-old now, and it kicked off in 2021 when EA hired Byron Beede, former boss of all of Call of Duty at Activision, to lead the next evolution of Battlefield. So far, that decision has given us the very successful Battlefield 6 and its free-to-play, COD: Warzone-like battle royale mode Redsec.

articles.title: 7 Upcoming Sci-Fi Series, Ranked By Hype (2026 and Early 2027)
articles.summary: Sci-fi is also as versatile as it gets. Shows like Paradise blend action-thriller elements with a puzzle-box narrative that sparks enthusiastic theorycrafting and discussion.
body: Why do sci-fi shows generate such massive hype? A select few, like Fallout or Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, bank on pre-existing fanbases, but most genre titles are highly anticipated purely due to their exciting premise. Stories about technological collapse or corporate overreach feel urgent and relevant, while dystopian cautionary tales are a fun way to explore speculative scenarios. Sci-fi also promises intricate world-building, be it through grounded space settings like The Expanse or alternative timeline tales like For All Mankind.

Ridley Scott’s Blade Runner paved the way for commercially viable cyberpunk media, becoming one of the most influential sci-fi movies of all time. Its sequel, Blade Runner 204 9, etched a flawed legacy with an interesting continuation of its complex themes. Prime Video’s upcoming series, Blade Runner 2099, presents a unique scenario: What would the world look like when the replicants take over?

articles.title: WoW: Forever's continued to wrestle with dungeons, as Blizzard admits it briefly 'missed the mark' on hotfixes over the weekend
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever 's been pretty great. At this point, I have around 150 hours played, a terrible posture problem, and a level 47 warrior I just barely avoided doing a 2 am Zul'Farrak run with yesterday. Speaking of, there has been a point of contention: Dungeons.
body: My position on the debate is fairly neutral —I think you could maybe bump up the mob XP by around 10% as a compromise—but overall I think they're fine. The new ones are bangers, and I get a huge bunch of XP from doing them at least once. Blizzard's recent choices, however, did have me scratching my head over the weekend.

For a short time, via a hotfix, enemies in dungeons wouldn't give experience points to anyone in the group if they were trivial (that is, greyed out) to at least one party member. On paper, this sounds incredibly reasonable. WoW has suffered from a plague of dungeon boosters (that is, people selling runs of dungeons to let folks AFK through their levelling journey) particularly in Classic.

But the moment you take a second to stare at how Classic dungeons are designed, you start to see the cracks form. Uldaman, for instance, has a level range of 41-51 in my dungeon finder. Maraudon, 46-55. Then there's the issue of the Scarlet Monastery, whose entire gauntlet runs from level 30 to 44 and is often done in one big sweep by groups.
points: World of Warcraft: Forever 's been pretty great.

articles.title: 5 Funniest 'Peanuts' Comics About Dogs
articles.summary: Broadly speaking, there are three types of Peanuts comics. There are the funny ones, the sweet ones, and ones that are both funny and sweet. (And, let’s be honest, there are a good number of boring ones too.) But, very generally speaking, those are the three types of good Peanuts comics: funny…
body: I bring this up because my goal here is to find the five funniest Peanuts comics about dogs. Not like, just Peanuts comics “starring Snoopy,” even though all of them do, but comic strips that are actually about dogs and the nature of dogs in general, if that makes sense. So that means no Flying Ace or Joe Cool stuff. I love those, but I wanted to define this one pretty narrowly about “dogs” (which, I guess, is still pretty broad).

I also wanted to just go for the funny ones. These aren’t the sweet “go hug your dog” Peanuts comics, or even the sweet/funny ones that check all the boxes for Snoopy fans. I was determined to just find funny, dog-themed Peanuts comics which illustrate Charles Schulz’s impressive abilities as a joke-writer.

Dogs do live a pretty enviable life. They have no jobs, people bring them food for free, and simple pleasures like stick-throwing are entirely fulfilling. A lot of people wish life was that simple for them — I know I do. Here, Snoopy addresses those feelings of jealousy many humans have towards dogs and basically says “Yeah, being a dog is pretty great.”

articles.title: Influential Warhammer miniature designer Aly Morrison has died
articles.summary: Miniature designer and artist Aly Morrison has died, as confirmed by Trish Carden Miniatures and Design on Facebook. Carden, Morrison's ex-wife and former partner in Marauder Miniatures, posted that, "Mharaid and I are heartbroken to announce the passing of Aly Morrison, a very much loved father…
body: Aly Morrison began sculpting for Citadel in 1983 as a freelancer before joining the studio full-time in 1986. He and Trish were then made stewards of Games Workshop's imprint Marauder Miniatures in 1988, where they had free reign to create quirky and characterful figures like the mohawked dwarf trollslayers and the giant with a whaler's beard and a booze barrel strapped to his waist that became archetypal parts of Warhammer.

Morrison also crafted the first miniatures for Blood Bowl players and drew the tokens to represent them in the board game's first edition. During his time at Games Workshop every faction from dark elves to space marines eventually benefited from his touch.

He's also well-regarded as a painter, and his reliance on a dark wash with a hint of purple in it jokingly known as "Aly's Brown Liquid" was legendary. He continued working on the recipe over the years, with a recent iteration described on his blog in 2020 if you want to whip some up yourself.

body: Season 5 of the free-to-play strange worlds survival game, Once Human, drops on November 18 (PT).
Look up to the sky. A gargantuan pipe-organ leviathan now commands the horizon of Once Human. It is always watching, always listening, and its mood dictates the apocalypse below.

videos.title: Metro 2033/Last Light: PS5/Pro/Xbox Series X|S Upgrade Tested - Can All Consoles Run at 120Hz?
body: To stoke excitement for the impending Metro 2039, 4A Games revisits the first two games in the series with a 4K and 60FPS upgrade on PS5 and Xbox Series X. Texture quality is boosted, and ambient occlusion is improved - and there's even a 120Hz mode to further sweeten the deal (at a resolution hit). Tom runs through all the improvements compared to the last-gen release.
